hero.title: Run your Discord server without leaving a settings page open.
hero.lead: {brand} handles moderation, welcomes, levels, tickets and giveaways across every server you manage. Change a setting here or with a slash command — both always show the same live state.

modules.title: Turn on what you need, ignore the rest
modules.lead: Each module is off until you enable it, and each one has its own page with a live preview of whatever {brand} will post.

moderation.title: Moderation
moderation.body: Warn, timeout, kick and ban with a reason attached. Warning escalation runs the punishment ladder for you.

automod.title: AutoMod
automod.body: Rules for invites, spam, links and words, with a playground that shows which rules a sample message trips.

welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.body: Greet new members with plain text or an embed, and hand out their first roles on the way in.

levels.title: Levels
levels.body: XP from messages and voice, role rewards per level, and a leaderboard your members can actually see.

tickets.title: Tickets
tickets.body: Panels that open a private channel, with a form builder, transcripts and auto-close.

giveaways.title: Giveaways
giveaways.body: Entry requirements by role or level, bonus entries, live countdowns and a one-click reroll.

mirror.title: The dashboard and the slash commands are the same thing
mirror.lead: Your moderators live in Discord and never open a browser. You want a real settings page. Both write to the same state, so neither view is ever stale — and if someone changes a setting while your form is open, {brand} tells you instead of overwriting it.
mirror.saveBar: Nothing auto-saves. A save bar names how many settings changed before anything reaches your server.
mirror.conflict: If a slash command changes the same setting while your form is open, the bar offers Reload or Keep mine.
mirror.audit: Every change is in the audit log with the actor, a before/after diff and whether it came from Web or Slash.

help.title: Help before you need it, and a human when you do
help.lead: Every module page links straight to its own docs page. If something is genuinely broken, the support server is the fastest route.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.body: Setup guides and a page per module, with the exact permissions each one needs.

support.title: Support server
support.body: Ask in Discord and get an answer from someone who works on the bot.

commands.title: Command reference
commands.body: Every slash command with its usage, required permission and cooldown.

status.title: Status & incidents
status.body: Live shard health, latency and a history of anything that went wrong.

free.question: Is it free?
free.answer: Yes, on unlimited servers. Pro raises the module limits — more AutoMod rules, more custom commands, longer audit retention — and Ultimate adds the economy module.

administrator.question: Do I need to give it Administrator?
administrator.answer: No. {brand} asks for the permissions each module needs, and the dashboard tells you exactly which permission is missing where you make the choice — not after you save.

slash.question: What happens if my moderators use slash commands instead?
slash.answer: Nothing breaks. Both write the same state, and every change lands in the audit log tagged Web or Slash so you can see where it came from.

export.question: Can I export my configuration?
export.answer: Yes. Settings export to a single file, and importing shows a diff of what would change before anything is applied.

cta.title: Add {brand} to a server in about a minute
cta.lead: Free on unlimited servers. The setup wizard walks you through the log channel and moderator roles, and you can skip it.

footer.tagline: A configuration dashboard for a Discord bot that stays in sync with your slash commands.
